name: Warcraft
description: Where to start Warcraft, what to skip, and the characters and events worth knowing before you play.
intro: Choose the adventure you want. The strategy campaigns, modern MMO, and Classic offer different ways into the same world. You can enjoy any of them without completing decades of games.
recommendation: For a focused character story, begin with Warcraft III. For the MMO, follow modern WoW’s new-player path and join the current campaign. Use the recaps to fill gaps as they become relevant.
basics: Azeroth is the main world. Draenor is the orcs’ original home; a portal connects their histories.
These are changing coalitions of peoples, not permanent labels for good and evil. They fight each other and sometimes cooperate.
The Legion is a demonic invading force; the Scourge is an undead army; the Void represents a different cosmic danger. Their stories overlap, but they are not interchangeable.

entries.title: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos
entries.audience: I want a story with memorable characters
entries.why: Its tutorial and connected campaigns introduce the people whose choices shape later Warcraft. It supplies a satisfying beginning without two older games of preparation.
entries.need: Orcs came from Draenor, lost a war against the Alliance, and now seek a future on Azeroth. The Legion is a demonic threat.
entries.skip: Warcraft I and II, WoW, novels, and comics. Read their short recaps only if you become curious.
entries.tradeoff: This is a strategy game with armies and missions. It introduces the world through its leaders rather than a custom adventurer.
entries.next: Play The Frozen Throne next. Stop there for a complete strategy-era journey, or follow one character into WoW.

entries.title: Modern World of Warcraft
entries.audience: I want an MMO I can join today
entries.why: The current new-player experience teaches your class and leads through a modern introduction. You can reach today’s shared adventure without clearing every old zone or raid.
entries.need: Start with the new-player path offered in game, including Dragonflight where directed. Alliance and Horde are coalitions; Azeroth faces threats larger than either.
entries.skip: Clearing old expansions in release order, collecting everything, and buying lore books.
entries.tradeoff: The MMO tells stories across quests, cinematics, and raids. Old campaigns are not one seamless sequence, and access to the latest expansion is separate from learning the world.
entries.next: Join Midnight when your character is ready. Use the saga recap below; choose The War Within first if you want the arc’s beginning.

entries.title: The War Within
entries.audience: I want to follow the current story from its beginning
entries.why: It starts the Worldsoul Saga and makes Azeroth’s own fate the focus. A short character recap is a smaller commitment than replaying the previous ten expansions.
entries.need: Azeroth has a world-soul. Alleria uses the Void, Anduin is recovering from trauma, and Xal’atath is gathering forces.
entries.skip: Full playthroughs of Battle for Azeroth, Shadowlands, and Dragonflight. Their recaps supply the relevant bridge.
entries.tradeoff: This is still WoW: character requirements and campaign access apply. A lore entry point is not a promise that a fresh character can immediately enter every quest.
entries.next: Follow the main campaign, then Midnight. Return to older regions only when their stories interest you.

entries.title: World of Warcraft Classic
entries.audience: I want to discover a world slowly
entries.why: Local quests and travel let you learn Azeroth through your own adventurer. Prior knowledge of Warcraft III is useful, but unnecessary.
entries.need: The factions are rebuilding after major wars. Pick a race and class that interest you and learn their home region.
entries.skip: Strategy games, modern expansion campaigns, and a checklist of raids.
entries.tradeoff: Classic’s rules and pace differ from modern WoW. Choose the Classic version your friends play; it is not a required first step before retail.
entries.next: Continue through the zones you enjoy, or move to modern WoW later with a short lore recap.

events.title: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans
events.premise: An invading orc army crosses a magical gateway into the human kingdom of Stormwind.
events.recap: Stormwind falls. Survivors flee north, turning a local invasion into a threat that other kingdoms must answer. Later Warcraft stories establish this outcome; the original two campaigns offer incompatible victories.
events.why: Recap it unless you enjoy early strategy games. The portal and the fall of Stormwind are the useful foundations.

events.title: Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness
events.premise: Human kingdoms and their allies unite against the expanding Horde.
events.recap: The Alliance defeats the Horde. The surviving orcs face captivity, while the struggle reaches beyond a single human kingdom.
events.why: A good optional visit for military history, naval campaigns, and the origins of the Alliance.

events.title: Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal
events.premise: An Alliance expedition crosses the portal to confront danger on the orcs’ homeworld.
events.recap: Ner’zhul opens additional portals and shatters Draenor. The expedition closes the connection to Azeroth, leaving its heroes stranded beyond it. The broken world becomes Outland.
events.why: This explains Outland and why Khadgar and Alleria have histories far from home. A recap is enough for most newcomers.

events.title: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos
events.premise: A spreading plague, a demonic invasion, and rival peoples force Azeroth’s leaders to choose who they can trust.
events.recap: Arthas takes Frostmourne and becomes a death knight, destroying the kingdom he meant to protect. Thrall builds a new Horde. Humans, orcs, and night elves unite at Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde. Sylvanas is killed and raised into undeath.
events.why: The strongest introduction to Warcraft’s recurring characters. Play the tutorial and campaigns in their intended order.

events.title: Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne
events.premise: The survivors of the war pursue competing futures across Azeroth and Outland.
events.recap: Sylvanas breaks free and leads the Forsaken. Illidan establishes himself in Outland, then loses to Arthas at Icecrown. Arthas reaches the Frozen Throne and becomes the Lich King. Rexxar’s campaign helps establish the Horde’s home in Durotar.
events.why: Play after Reign of Chaos. It is the bridge to WoW and several of its major character arcs.

events.title: World of Warcraft
events.premise: Years after the Third War, adventurers explore a fragile world whose local dangers hide larger threats.
events.recap: The Alliance and Horde consolidate their communities while adventurers confront threats including Ragnaros, the black dragonflight, the qiraji, and the Scourge. There is no single compulsory campaign connecting every zone.
events.why: Choose Classic for the slower discovery of a world. You do not need to finish its raids before playing modern WoW.

events.title: The Burning Crusade
events.premise: The Dark Portal reopens, bringing adventurers to a ruined world contested by demons and rival rulers.
events.recap: Illidan is defeated at the Black Temple. Kael’thas’s alliance with the Legion leads to a confrontation at the Sunwell, where Kil’jaeden’s arrival is stopped and the Sunwell is restored.
events.why: An optional follow-up to Illidan’s Warcraft III story. Its finale is separate from the Black Temple arc.

events.title: Wrath of the Lich King
events.premise: The campaign against the Scourge takes the factions to the frozen north.
events.recap: Arthas is defeated at Icecrown Citadel. Bolvar Fordragon takes the helm to contain the Scourge, showing that killing its ruler does not simply erase the undead threat.
events.why: The most direct WoW continuation of Arthas’s story. For this character route, Warcraft III matters more than playing every earlier expansion.

events.title: Cataclysm
events.premise: Deathwing’s return transforms familiar lands and draws the dragon Aspects into a struggle for survival.
events.recap: Deathwing is defeated with the aid of Thrall and the dragon Aspects. Azeroth survives, but its geography and the dragons’ role have changed.
events.why: Recap the world’s transformation. Explore it if the altered zones or dragon history interest you.

events.title: Mists of Pandaria
events.premise: The Alliance and Horde bring their conflict to a land where destructive emotions can become tangible threats.
events.recap: Garrosh’s rule drives a rebellion within the Horde. Alliance forces and Horde rebels defeat him in the Siege of Orgrimmar. Pandaria’s sha make the cost of the faction war visible.
events.why: A strong optional regional adventure. The Garrosh recap is the bridge to Warlords of Draenor.

events.title: Warlords of Draenor
events.premise: An alternate version of the orcs’ homeworld becomes the staging ground for an Iron Horde invasion.
events.recap: Garrosh’s intervention creates a different path for Draenor’s clans. The Iron Horde gives way to a Legion threat; this timeline’s Gul’dan ultimately reaches the main Azeroth.
events.why: Recap this for Legion. This is an alternate-history branch reached after Pandaria, not a replacement for the original First War.

events.title: Legion
events.premise: A renewed demonic invasion sends Azeroth’s defenders to the Broken Isles and beyond.
events.recap: The campaign reaches Argus. The Legion’s leadership is overcome and Sargeras is imprisoned, but his sword wounds Azeroth. Illidan remains behind as Sargeras’s jailer. Anduin inherits the throne after Varian’s death.
events.why: A substantial optional story for Illidan and the Legion. Its aftermath explains Azeroth’s wound and the next faction conflict.

events.title: Battle for Azeroth
events.premise: The factions seek powerful allies while the consequences of Azeroth’s wound fuel another war.
events.recap: Sylvanas burns Teldrassil, and the war divides the Horde as well as the factions. Her rule ends after Saurfang’s challenge. The campaign also confronts Azshara and N’Zoth, while Xal’atath gains freedom from her dagger.
events.why: Recap the faction rupture and Azeroth’s wound before the Worldsoul Saga. Play the regions if naval kingdoms and faction politics appeal to you.

events.title: Shadowlands
events.premise: A breach between the living world and the afterlife draws Azeroth’s heroes into the realms of the dead.
events.recap: The Jailer’s plan is defeated and Anduin is freed from domination. Sylvanas is sentenced to recover souls from the Maw. Anduin’s experiences leave lasting wounds that matter when he returns in The War Within.
events.why: A short recap supplies the character context for Anduin and Sylvanas. It is not required homework before modern WoW.

events.title: Dragonflight
events.premise: The dragonflights return to their ancestral home as old enemies challenge their legacy.
events.recap: The dragonflights resist the Primal Incarnates. Amirdrassil survives Fyrakk’s assault and the Aspects regain their power through Azeroth. The story restores a sense of home while threats around Iridikron point toward the Void.
events.why: A welcoming modern leveling introduction. Follow its main campaign and leave completion of every reputation and side quest for later.

events.title: The War Within
events.premise: A call from Azeroth draws adventurers beneath the surface to Khaz Algar, where Xal’atath is gathering allies.
events.recap: At the opening of the saga, Dalaran is attacked and the heroes enter Khaz Algar. Anduin’s recovery and Alleria’s struggle with the Void become central character threads. This guide covers the expansion’s setup rather than every patch resolution.
events.why: Start here for the beginning of the current multi-expansion arc, with the short background recap instead of a tour of all older expansions.

events.title: Midnight
events.premise: Xal’atath’s assault turns attention to Quel’Thalas and the struggle against the Void.
events.recap: The released expansion begins with the defence of Quel’Thalas and the threat of the Voidstorm. Coverage here stops at the launch premise; it does not predict the outcome of the ongoing expansion or its later patches.
events.why: Choose this to play alongside the current community. Catch up on The War Within first, then follow the in-game campaign.

events.title: The Last Titan
events.premise: The announced final chapter of the Worldsoul Saga turns toward Northrend and the titans.
events.why: An announced destination, not a playable entry point. No ending or release date is assumed here.

characters.name: Arthas Menethil
characters.motivation: Protecting his people becomes inseparable from his need to defeat their enemies.
characters.relationships: Jaina is a close personal connection; Uther is his mentor.

updates.text: His pursuit of the plague leads him to Frostmourne and service as a death knight.
He defeats Illidan at Icecrown and takes the Lich King’s helm.
His reign ends at Icecrown Citadel. Bolvar inherits the burden of containing the Scourge.

characters.name: Thrall
characters.motivation: He wants his people to build a future beyond captivity and demonic control.
characters.relationships: Grom Hellscream is a formative ally; Jaina becomes an important bridge between peoples.

updates.text: He leads the orcs to Kalimdor and allies with former enemies against the Legion.
He works with the dragon Aspects to oppose Deathwing.
Garrosh’s rule exposes the limits of the future Thrall had hoped to build.

characters.name: Jaina Proudmoore
characters.motivation: She weighs loyalty to her people against the possibility of peace with their enemies.
characters.relationships: Her history with Arthas and her alliance with Thrall pull her loyalties in different directions.

updates.text: She refuses to follow Arthas’s increasingly ruthless path and later joins the defence of Hyjal.
The destruction of Theramore hardens her view of the Horde.
Returning to Kul Tiras forces her to confront her family and the cost of earlier choices.

characters.name: Sylvanas Windrunner
characters.motivation: Her story concerns survival, autonomy, and what those aims can justify.
characters.relationships: Alleria and Vereesa are her sisters.

updates.text: Arthas kills her and forces her into undeath.
She wins freedom and leads the Forsaken.
Her choices as warchief culminate in Teldrassil’s destruction and a rebellion against her.
Her pact with the Jailer ends; she accepts penance in the Maw.

characters.name: Illidan Stormrage
characters.role: A night elf willing to wield dangerous power
characters.motivation: He believes conventional restraint can prevent victory over an existential enemy.
characters.relationships: Malfurion is his brother; Tyrande is central to their shared history.

updates.text: Tyrande releases him to fight the Legion, but his use of demonic power brings renewed exile.
He rules in Outland and fails to defeat Arthas.
Adventurers defeat him at the Black Temple.
He returns to the struggle against the Legion and stays to guard Sargeras.

characters.name: Tyrande Whisperwind
characters.role: A night elf leader and priestess
characters.motivation: She seeks to protect her people while balancing faith, duty, and grief.
characters.relationships: Malfurion is her partner; her decisions also shape Illidan’s path.

updates.text: She brings the night elves into the alliance that defends Mount Hyjal.
Teldrassil’s destruction turns her story toward vengeance.
Amirdrassil becomes a new hope for her people.

characters.name: Anduin Wrynn
characters.role: A human royal with a talent for healing
characters.motivation: He tries to reconcile responsibility, compassion, and the expectations of leadership.
characters.relationships: Varian is his father; Jaina and the other Alliance leaders help shape his outlook.

updates.text: He becomes king after Varian’s death.
The Jailer dominates him; being freed does not end the emotional consequences.
His return centres on recovering his confidence and connection to the Light.

characters.name: Alleria Windrunner
characters.motivation: She fights to protect her home while living with dangerous sources of power.
characters.relationships: Sylvanas and Vereesa are her sisters; Turalyon and Arator are her closest family.

updates.text: She is stranded beyond the portal with the expedition.
She returns after a long struggle against the Legion, now wielding the Void.
Xal’atath tests her command of that power and her sense of identity.

characters.name: Khadgar
characters.motivation: He looks for cooperation and knowledge capable of stopping threats larger than any one kingdom.
characters.relationships: Medivh is his former teacher; Alleria and Turalyon are expedition companions.

updates.text: The expedition leaves him on the shattered world that becomes Outland.
He helps coordinate the campaign against the Legion.
The attack on Dalaran removes a familiar source of guidance at the saga’s opening.

characters.name: Xal’atath
characters.role: A mysterious figure associated with the Void
characters.motivation: She exploits other people’s ambitions and vulnerabilities in pursuit of her own designs.
characters.relationships: Alleria is a central opponent in the Worldsoul Saga.

updates.text: She escapes the dagger that had bound her.
As the Harbinger, she gathers forces beneath Azeroth.

factions: A coalition whose human, dwarven, elven, and other members do not always agree. Follow its internal arguments as well as its war with the Horde.
A coalition shaped by displacement, survival, and arguments about honour and leadership. It changes markedly from the invading Horde of the early games.
A demonic army that threatens multiple worlds. Warcraft III and Legion offer the clearest focused route into this conflict.
Dragon communities with distinct responsibilities and histories. Dragonflight introduces their present-day concerns.
A cosmic force whose influence matters increasingly in the Worldsoul Saga. Alleria and Xal’atath provide two very different points of contact.
scope: Covers Warcraft I–III and their story expansions, original WoW, and every released WoW expansion through Midnight. The Last Titan is announced. Modern expansion coverage is an orientation, not a patch-by-patch chronicle; The War Within and Midnight entries focus on their opening premises. Classic rereleases are alternate ways to play existing eras. Hearthstone, Warcraft Rumble, novels, and the film are outside this game-story route. Later lore may revise early accounts.
